title: unified-rollouts-weighted-canary-shadow-ab-auto-rollback-policy
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: We need a single rollout primitive that supports weighted canary, A/B, and shadow traffic patterns while providing automated multi-metric rollback for production model rollouts. Current code paths are fragmented (canary vs shadow vs ab) and don't support composite policies or coordinated rollbacks across metrics (latency, error-rate, quality regressions). This PR introduces a unified rollout policy and controller that: 1) supports weight-driven canary and A/B experiments, 2) allows shadow-only traffic to run side-by-side for non-invasive evaluation, and 3) evaluates multiple metrics with configurable thresholds and cooldown windows to trigger automated rollback. What changed (high level): Added a new rollout policy (WeightedCanaryShadowPolicy) in core/rollouts that orchestrates traffic split, collects metric evaluations, and triggers rollback when thresholds are exceeded. Introduced a policy config schema for model lifecycle manifests to declare rollout strategy, metric buckets, evaluation windows, and fallback models. Updated the API surface (api/v1/rollouts.yaml) to accept the new policy spec and added SDK helpers for creating weighted rollouts. Added end-to-end tests and integration harness updates. Design notes: The policy runs as a stateful controller which manages two kinds of traffic: "live" (serving traffic subject to weight changes) and "shadow" (duplicate requests sent to candidate models with no user-visible response). We evaluate a configurable metric set: p95 latency, 5xx error rate, and a lightweight quality signal (approx-match ratio from eval hooks). Each metric has a warning and critical threshold. Warning triggers pause and alert; critical triggers rollback. The controller uses a sliding window aggregator and requires sustained breach over N consecutive windows before taking action to reduce flapping. Rollback is executed by promoting the last-known-good model and optionally draining in-flight requests using configured grace periods. Rollout strategy & API compatibility: Existing rollout manifests that use legacy canary/ab semantics will continue to work. New manifests can opt into the WeightedCanaryShadowPolicy using the new "strategy.type: weighted_canary_shadow" field and parameters: initial_weight, step_size, evaluation_window_seconds, metrics[], shadow: true|false, rollback_policy. The system supports both gradual weight ramps and single-step promotions. Testing & validation: Unit tests for policy logic (tests/rollouts/test_weighted_canary.py), integration tests exercising controller + routing, and a perf canary to validate scheduling overhead. CI added a new matrix job to run rollout integration tests against a lightweight local runtime. Performed staged rollout in staging cluster, then canaryed on a small production shard for 24h before full rollout. Observability: new dashboards (Grafana) and alerts added to monitor policy decisions and rollback events. Checklist: - [x] Design doc written and reviewed (link: https://linear.app/ENG/2945) - [x] Policy implementation in core/rollouts - [x] API spec changes and SDK helpers - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Perf canary + staging validation - [x] Docs: docs/unified-rollouts.md updated - [x] Feature flagged behind rollout.unified_policy.v1 Related: builds on previous work in PRs: pr-52310, pr-53678, pr-46821. Linear: ENG-2945 (design), ENG-3010 (rollout automation).
